title: Grok Bot Games Development
author: Beginning-Sign1916
selftext: Recently I have been seeing quite a few recommended videos related to Grok Bot and after looking into it just a curious part has anyone use Grok Bot to develop a game even if it's a simple three.js or do you guys just use claude or codex and create multi agents to fine tune, review and run test on your game?

comments.author: Melodic-Chemistry127
comments.body: It's going to be okay-ish for small games and experiments. You'll need a serious model for serious work, though.

comments.author: cckynv
comments.body: Honestly, I don’t think you could pay me to use Grok.

replies.author: svj1794
replies.body: That sounds personal care to expand? Why ? Or what you do use.

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: Partially just don’t like Elon and don’t want to support him. Partially Grok is just overall inferior from what I can tell to any of the models I currently use (I work within Anthropic’s ecosystem at the moment).

replies.author: svj1794
replies.body: Gottcha whats the jist of what you're making or doing with itand what hardware are you running to do that? Anthropic ecosystem care to expand on what you actually use of theirs?

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body:
I'm making a 3D game, a co-op action RPG set in a world I've been working on for a couple years. Hardware-wise all consumer grade tech, I'm not running anything super high-end and don't really need to because I'm not running local models. What I meant by Anthropic ecosystem was that I'm using solely their models in Claude Code. Mostly Opus 5.5 with a mix of Fable 5.1 and Sonnet 5.5 for different types of tasks. Using the Unity plugin for Claude Code along with the Unity CLI and pipeline package to drive the Unity Editor.

Also working on a couple browser-based games but a majority of my time/tokens is spent on the RPG. Some webdev on the side too.

replies.author: svj1794
replies.body: Thats awesome i would like to make a 3d game also i have almost no experience with this stuff .  Need a tester lol claude does that huh

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: Yeah Claude is great for game dev and coding in general. Give it a shot, I think you’ll be impressed. It can even help you with automated testing and then hand off more visual/feel-based judgements for you to decide on.

replies.author: svj1794
replies.body: Copy . I have wanted to try out claude or gpt . Would you still reccomend the claude over say gpts astra?

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: For the coding and game design side of things, 100% Claude. The only notable thing that I think GPT models do better is generating art/graphics, although Claude + Blender MCP is more than capable at the moment at generating assets, it just might take a little more iteration on average.

replies.author: svj1794
replies.body: I would love to trial it but honestly wouldn't know where to start

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: I can DM you the trial pass if you’d like, just let me know. As for where to start, if you have a basic idea for a game, start with prompting Claude to help you develop a game design document and/or an implementation plan. Then you can ask how to set up your workspace in Unity/UE/GoDot depending on which game engine you decide to use.

replies.author: svj1794
replies.body: Ill take it please. What other gamedev tools would you reccomend?

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: Sent it to you in a DM. As for other tools, it really just depends on what you want to make. Blender is probably good to get if you want to make a 3D game. Things like Aesprite are really good for 2D/pixel art. You can make custom tooling with AI quite easily as well, to fit your specific use cases.

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: Also, if you just want to give Claude a test run, I can hook you up with a 7-day trial pass if you’d like.
